https://www.dw.com/en/sudan-us-proposes-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JKwq Observers say weaponry is getting more sophisticated on both sides of the conflict in Sudan [FILE: Aug 30, 2023] Image: AFP Advertisement The United States on Monday proposed expanding an existing UN arms embargo for Darfur to cover all of Sudan . The proposal was put forth by US Envoy Massad Boulos during a UN Security Council meeting in New York. "The brutality of the war waged by the Rapid Support Forces [RSF] and the Sudanese Armed Forces has discredited their claims to be legitimate governors of the Sudanese people," said Boulos, who warned that "external financial and military support is fueling the conflict and risks drawing neighboring states deeper into war." Boulos said the US wants to expand the embargo geographically as well as materially in order to cover unmanned aerial vehicles and related technologies . Moreover, the US plan would see the number of experts monitoring the embargo increased. The Darfur embargo has been in place for two decades and will expire on September 12, 2026, if not amended or renewed. An expansion would require a Security Council vote. Sudan wants 'technical extension' but warns against hampering army Sudan's UN envoy urged members to endorse a "technical extension" of the existing embargo while warning against changes that would hamper the army. "Sudan suffers the most from weapons and their illegal flow. However, expanding such a sanctions regime will weaken the protection of civilians," said Al-Harith Idriss al-Harith Mohamed. Russia , which holds veto powers in the Security Council, has voiced skepticism over changes to the existing deal, saying that expanding the embargo could impact the Sudanese army's effectiveness. Escaping death in Sudan's civil war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video UN Sudan experts say sophisticated weaponry suggests 'external support' Before Boulos articulated the US position, UN Under Secretary General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary Di Carlo warned that a "worrying aspect of the conflict in Sudan is its increasing complexity." "Sophisticated weaponry," she said, "continues to point to ongoing external support to both parties." The UN's humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, also made note of the fact that, "in recent weeks, fighting in Sudan has been characterized by the heavy use of drones and localized ground combat in areas less affected by rainy season conditions." The war in Sudan , now in its fourth year, has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions of civilians. While Sudan's army holds sway in the country's central and eastern regions, western and parts of southern Darfur are under control of rival Rapid Support Forces . Darfur, a vast western region the size of France, has seen some of the worst violence of the conflict, with repeated attacks on displacement camps and ethnic massacres that kill thousands at a time . Is Sudan's next mass atrocity already underway? https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/30/came.text: A Cameroonian group known as "Bring Back Our Sons and Brothers" is calling on both Russia and Cameroon to work together to dismantle covert recruitment networks that have been enlisting Cameroonians into the Russian army to fight in Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.The collective organised a peaceful march to the Russian Embassy on Wednesday as Cameroonians took to the streets of the country's capital, Yaoundé, to protest such schemes."This march aims to draw the attention of two friendly nations - Russia and Cameroon - urging them to do everything in their power to dismantle the clandestine network that continues to drain Cameroon of its sons," Paul Sylvain Yede, one of the group's cofounders, said.According to a report by the collective "All Eyes on Wagner," at least 1,417 Africans have been recruited into the ranks of the Russian military, with more than 300 reported dead.Lured by the promise of employment in Russia, these young men have instead found themselves thrust onto the front lines in Ukraine, where Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022.Catherine Djock has been waiting for news of her husband for the best part of a year after he travelled to Russia to take up what he thought would be work in a kitchen."For nine months, I have had no information about my husband’s situation - whether he is alive or not. I cannot accept that he is dead, as I have not seen his body; therefore, I believe he is still alive," she said."If he is alive, I want Russia to bring my husband back to me. He was supposed to work as a cook, but upon his arrival, he ended up on the front lines. I want the truth about my husband. That is why I have come out today."Ngong San Djombi, the father of a victim, added: "I lost a son - the youngest of my five children. I demand that my son be returned to me, regardless of his condition - even if he is disabled. I cannot accept being told he is gone when I haven’t seen his body. I have refused to hold a funeral; I have simply prayed."

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjdx.text: Image source, Site PÃ´le Jean Moulin Image caption, Solange Alexandre twice turned down the LÃ©gion d'Honneur before relenting in 2024 By Hugh Schofield in Paris Published 1 hour ago One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters. After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of RuillÃ©-sur-Loir. With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces. President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans. "She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media. Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, nÃ©e Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One. "My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs. In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter. "From that moment I knew I had to join up," she wrote. Some months later she was recruited by a friend of her father's â a Tunisian-born French army veteran called SaÃ¯d Belhaffaf, who had joined the Resistance. Using the code-name Corlay, she criss-crossed the region around Le Mans by bicycle, gathering information and passing on messages. "There were no mobile phones back then, and no private cars either because of the lack of petrol. The bicycle was king," she said in an interview two years ago. In 1943 she met her first husband Guy DÃ©liot, who had deserted from the French gendarmerie after refusing to arrest some Jews. The following April, with the Allied invasion approaching, they decided to take to the maquis, in other words live clandestinely in the forested hills, supplied with food by local farmers. Their group consisted of deserters from German forced labour programmes, as well as survivors from another Resistance outfit that had been destroyed by the enemy. There were also two airmen, one American and one Canadian. "Twice the Gestapo came for me, and twice I slipped through their hands," she later recalled. After taking part in the liberation of Tours in September 1944, she ended the war with the rank of sub-lieutenant in the French Interior Forces (FFI). Later she worked as a teacher and followed her husband on his many postings as an officer of the gendarmerie in French overseas territories. He was killed in 1960 in Martinique, and in 1981 she remarried. Twice Solange Alexandre turned down the LÃ©gion d'Honneur , saying that she had only done her duty and that others were more worthy. Finally in 2024 she relented. On receiving the award she said: "It is a great pleasure and a great honour. I am very proud â even if it is only a few weeks, or a few months, before I die." https://hotnews.ro/cum-isi-pregatesc-pro.text: Trei cazuri care arată cât de greu poate fi să recunoști un abuz atunci când persoana de care ar trebui să te ferești este chiar profesorul tău. Anul acesta, un profesor de geografie din Bacău a fost arestat pentru că a violat o elevă, căreia îi trimitea mesaje de dragoste și materiale pornografice. La Cernavodă, un alt profesor a fost acuzat de viol asupra unei minore, după ce, potrivit procurorilor, ar fi creat o relație de dependență afectivă cu aceasta. La Iași, șapte studente l-au acuzat pe lectorul universitar Alexandru Toader că ar fi profitat de dificultățile lor la examene pentru a le chema la întâlniri private. „Să nu vorbești cu necunoscuți”, „Să nu accepți invitații suspecte”, „Să pleci dacă te simți în pericol”. Sunt avertismente pe care părinții le repetă copiilor, cu convingerea că astfel îi pot proteja. Dar ce se întâmplă când adultul care depășește limitele este un profesor? Când de el depinde promovarea unui examen sau când copilul are încredere în el și nu își dă seama că apropierea a devenit nepotrivită? Mesaje intime, dependență emoțională, presiuni legate de examene: cazurile din Bacău, Cernavodă și Iași arată că abuzul poate veni și de la omul aflat la catedră. De aceea, elevii și studenții trebuie să recunoască semnalele de alarmă, să știe că pot refuza solicitările nepotrivite și pot cere ajutor indiferent cine este adultul implicat, ce funcție are sau cât de respectat este. Uneori, abuzul sexual este precedat de o apropiere treptată: adultul câștigă încrederea elevului, îi acordă atenție specială, îi oferă favoruri și încearcă să creeze o relație pe care o poate controla. Atunci când urmărește exploatarea sexuală a unui minor, acest proces este numit grooming . Psiholoaga Mihaela Dinu de la Salvați Copiii a explicat cum câștigă agresorii încrederea minorilor, prezentându-se drept protectori, pentru ca apoi să folosească frica și amenințările pentru a-i controla.
